glosses: A faint, harsh sound made in the throat.
The call of a frog or toad.
The harsh call of various birds, such as the raven or corncrake, or other creatures.
To make a croak sound.
To utter in a low, hoarse voice.

examples.text: The raven himself is hoarse, / That croaks the fatal entrance of Duncan.

glosses: To make its vocal sound.
To die.
To kill someone or something.

examples.text: If Wilton croaked the criminal he did a jolly good day's work, and there's an end of it.
He'd seen my face, so I had to croak him.
"It was me. And I'm glad, damned glad, I didn't croak him. With this slick guy after me, it would be me for the chair."

glosses: To complain; especially, to grumble; to forebode evil; to utter complaints or forebodings habitually.

examples.text: Marat […] croaks with such reasonableness.

glosses: To abort the current program indicating a user or caller error.

examples.text: The accessor croaks if it's not an appropriate object reference.

examples.text: Im Gartenteich quakten munter die Frösche.

(Wildgans:) „Und auch wer genau hinhört, kann die verschiedenen Zugvögel oftmals identifizieren: Während Kraniche tiefe, trompetenartige Laute von sich geben, quaken Wildgänse in viel höherer Tonlage “
„Nilkrokodilmütter vergraben ihre Eier in der Erde. Die Jungen quaken beim Schlüpfen. Dies ist für die Mutter das Zeichen, das Nest aufzugraben.“

glosses: definizione mancante; se vuoi, aggiungila tu
The cry of a hen or goose, especially when laying an egg.

examples.text: I heard a grey hen cackling among the ling; I called and thought, "If I could get a sight of you now, it would be your last cackle;" just then I heard something moving behind me on the path.

glosses: A laugh resembling the cry of a hen or goose.
Futile or excessively noisy talk.

examples.text: There's no time to waste on silly cackle.

glosses: A group of hyenas.
To make a sharp, broken noise or cry, as a hen or goose does.

examples.text: When every goose is cackling.
I heard a grey hen cackling among the ling; I called and thought, "If I could get a sight of you now, it would be your last cackle;" just then I heard something moving behind me on the path.

glosses: To laugh with a broken sound similar to a hen's cry.

examples.text: The witch cackled evilly.

She was a fat, round little woman, richly apparelled in velvet and lace, […]; and the way she laughed, cackling like a hen, the way she talked to the waiters and the maid,[…]—all these unexpected phenomena impelled one to hysterical mirth, and made one class her with such immortally ludicrous types as Ally Sloper, the Widow Twankey, or Miss Moucher.

glosses: To talk in a silly manner; to prattle.

examples.text: It is also the business of a sensible government, not to cackle on its discoveries

glosses: To pretend to rattle (dice) in one's hand while gripping them so that they maintain their orientation.

examples.text: Danny cackled the dice furiously in his cupped hand, then rolled them so they stopped inches from Slattery's hands. The result was the same as before – a seven.

[…] they spun all right, or so it seemed, and hit the wall all right, or so it seemed, but bottom line was this: The stirring of the dice was merely cackling, the cubes artfully framed so that the spots in the kid's fists showed 4‐4 up‐right and weren't really rattled but rather, held in control by the pinky, forefinger and thumb; […]

glosses: äußern, rufen (eines Pferdes)

examples.text: Auf Wiesen kann man Pferde wiehern hören.

glosses: laut, hoch lachen

examples.text: Die Kinder wieherten vor Vergnügen.
